The Respondents are distribution licensees and power departments that procure transmission services from the Petitioner, mainly beneficiaries of the Northern Region. 5. The Petitioner has served the Petition on the Respondents, and notice regarding the filing of this Petition has also been published in newspapers in accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as the ‘Act’). No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the notice published in the newspapers by the Petitioner. 6. The hearing in this matter was held on various dates, and the order in the matter was reserved on 30.9.2024. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner through affidavits dated 25.4.2022, 30.11.2022, 19.12.2022, and 11.3.2024; NTPC’s reply filed through affidavit dated 27.1.2023; the Petitioner’s rejoinder to NTPC’s reply filed by NTPC vide affidavit dated 24.2.2023; CTUIL’s additional submissions filed vide affidavit dated 3.2.2023; and the revised additional submissions of CTUIL filed through affidavit dated 23.5.2023. 7. The Petitioner endeavoured to synchronise the commissioning of the transmission assets with that of the associated generators so that the assets could be put to intended use immediately upon commissioning. c. According to the Petitioner, the delay in commissioning of the assets was beyond its control and is covered under Regulation 22(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, and as such it should be condoned. _ii.
